children: A $664 billion contracted-revenue backlog lifted Oracle

, the database-software and cloud-infrastructure company, roughly 7% before Friday's opening bell. That excitement did not last. After reaching $165.80, the stock fell back to $153.74, trimming its gain to approximately 0.6%.

Oracle's fiscal first-quarter results delivered plenty of AI firepower. Revenue climbed 30% to $19.3 billion, while infrastructure-as-a-service revenue surged 121% to $7.4 billion. The company also added 850 megawatts of computing capacity, installed more than 300,000 GPUs and pushed remaining performance obligations to $664 billion.

That backlog is roughly 34 times quarterly revenue, signaling enormous demand but also a long road from signed contracts to reported sales. The picture adds a valuation twist: Oracle's $153.74 share price sits 21.26% below its GF Value of $195.24. Still, negative free cash flow of approximately $5.4 billion and plans to raise $40 billion this fiscal year explain the sharp reversalinvestors want proof that AI revenue can outrun the spending needed to build it.

title: Oracle Nearly Erases 7% Jump Despite $664 Billion AI Backlog
